title: Stomach flushing technique applied to quantify microplastics in Crocodilians
author: Gonzalez-Jauregui, Borges-Ramirez, et al.
materials: Microplastic extraction, identification and quantification.•Possible microplastic fragments were transferred back to petri dishes and each fragment was separated under a dissecting microscope (10×) or an illuminated magnifying glass (4×).•All suspected microplastic fragments were analysed in a Nicolet iS5 (Thermo) FTIR spectrophotometer in order to identify their composition. Microplastics were identified by OMNIC Software for FTIR Spectroscopy and its libraries.

steps.title: Capture and immobilize crocodile
steps.instruction: Capture crocodiles according to size: small individuals by hand, larger ones with stainless‑steel snares attached to an aluminium pole; then securely immobilize the animal.

steps.title: Insert PVC pipe and fix
steps.instruction: Manually open the jaws, insert a short PVC pipe sized to the crocodile, and fix it in place with red vinyl insulation tape.

steps.title: Introduce spoon and hose
steps.instruction: Raise the head 30° from the longitudinal axis, lubricate a copper spoon with mineral oil, and insert it through the PVC pipe and palatal valve using smooth rotational movements; choose spoon length appropriate to the animal’s size. When the spoon tip is felt near the hind limbs by lateral palpation, lubricate a silicone hose with mineral oil, select a hose diameter matching the crocodile size, and insert it to the stomach. Connect the external hose end to a funnel and pump deionized (purified) water into the stomach until full.

steps.title: Collect flushed contents
steps.instruction: Quickly withdraw the hose, tilt the crocodile 45° facing a collection bucket fitted with a stainless‑steel sieve, use the metallic spoon and manual stomach massages to aid expulsion of contents; repeat the water‑flushing cycle up to four times or until only water is expelled.

steps.title: Record animal measurements
steps.instruction: After flushing, identify each crocodile, determine sex by visual inspection of the cloaca, measure snout‑vent length and total length, and record body weight.

steps.title: Sieve stomach material
steps.instruction: Pass the collected stomach contents through a series of sieves of 4.75 mm, 2.36 mm, and 1 mm; retain material from each sieve, label it, and store it refrigerated; discard the remaining liquid appropriately.

steps.title: Microscopic sorting of fragments
steps.instruction: Transfer retained material to petri dishes, examine under a 40× microscope, and categorize items as (i) recognizable prey fragments, (ii) gastroliths or other natural materials, or (iii) possible microplastic fragments; collect and label the suspected microplastic pieces.

steps.title: FTIR analysis of microplastics
steps.instruction: Place each suspected microplastic fragment onto a petri dish and isolate it further under a dissecting microscope (10×) or illuminated magnifying glass (4×); analyse all fragments with a Nicolet iS5 (Thermo) FTIR spectrophotometer and identify polymer type using OMNIC Software for FTIR Spectroscopy and its libraries.
